agreed: ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 and scripts/CONTRACTS.md 6.1b, agreed with /execution (its ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2, 4.2, 6.6, 11 and 19) on 2026-10-01. /execution's generic UI template and its simple-UI path are dropped: the judged UI is built once, from these templates.
rules: Select: drop a template when the plan's mode is small and small_mode.include is false, or when params.references.<value>.include is false for the plan's references value.

Expand: instances per-group gives one task per feature group of the feature catalogue ({group} = the group id, {features} = its FR ids joined by commas, no spaces); single gives one task ({group} = all, {features} = every catalogue id). params.<param>.<value>.instances overrides instances.

Depend: dependencies are resolved at instantiation, never at runtime: depends plus params.<param>.<value>.depends for the plan's values. There is no OR and no conditional dependency. A dependency on a per-group template means every instance of it. decision:... and manual:... entries name tasks /execution creates (see symbolic_depends). covers.depends_on_covering_tasks adds every non-frontend task whose covers intersect {features} (the feature's own build task). When stacks[profile.frontend.stack].sections is serial, the first FE-1x instance also depends on FE-09 and each further instance on the one before it, in group order, so no two UI proofs share a file or the preview port at the same time.
Stack: apply stacks[profile.frontend.stack].replace to proof.spec and to every string of fragment.input, then add stacks[...].add_resources to every task whose proof.spec contains --serve or --start.
Substitute: placeholders are replaced verbatim and nothing is quoted on substitution, because the specs already quote every path placeholder. A placeholder left unreplaced is a planning error.

Proof: command specs run with the working directory at the root of the product repository checkout the verifier rebuilt from the landed commit (pre_t0 tasks run from the workspace root); frontend-check never builds, so UI specs chain the build first, and it exits 0 only when every requested gate is ok (a skipped gate exits 1). A file proof names a file and a JSON pointer whose value must meet expect.
Estimate: estimate.<mode> gives p10_min, p50_min and p90_min in minutes; estimate.verify is the verifier's re-run of the proof. Both are recalibrated by /execution after every wave.
Cover: covers.rule feature-group sets the task's covers to the FR ids of {group}; none sets no covers.

Run: runner agent is one implementer agent whose brief names every brief_refs path (no reliance on skill auto-loading). runner fragment: the wave emitter inlines fragment.file and awaits fragment.function(api, input) with fragment.input resolved, where a value {"$from": "<path>"} is read from the profile at emission; the function's return value is the task's receipt. runner owner: a manual or decision task; manual maps to plan.json manual {steps, bring_back, options_source, where} and /execution computes latest_start_utc and adds the human resource.
Refs: brief_refs never include references/11-tells.md; the catalogue of tells is for the checker, the critics and the reviewers only, because listing bad examples primes the builder (FD02-F33).

Prework: pre_t0 true means the task may run before kickoff as research, with {state} = <workspace.private_dir>/frontend, and its outputs are imported into .execution/frontend at T0; a task with pre_t0 false never runs before T0 when the event forbids designs.

Answers: H1, H2 and H3 reach /frontend only through {state}/choices.json (assets/schemas/choices.schema.json), written by the orchestrator from a Notion decision field or a Remote Control reply; canvas comments are not answers. The review board is published by the orchestrator in the main thread, never by a workflow agent (references/03-directions.md).

placeholders.{ui_root}: Repository-relative folder of the UI package (forward slashes, no trailing slash), set by the plan. Never '.' while other lanes write the repository, because FE-08 and FE-20 write {ui_root}/**.
placeholders.{group}: Feature group id of an FE-1x instance (G1, G2, ...), or all when the template runs as a single instance.
placeholders.{features}: Comma-separated FR ids of {group}, no spaces (FR-003,FR-007).
placeholders.{design}: Repository-relative design folder: profile.frontend.paths.design, default design.
placeholders.{state}: Absolute /frontend state directory: <main checkout>/.execution/frontend in mode A after T0, <workspace.private_dir>/frontend before T0. Absolute so a proof re-run from a clean checkout still finds it.
placeholders.{private_dir}: Absolute workspace.private_dir of the profile: captures of third-party sites live there, outside any git work tree, and are purged after the pattern ledger is written.
placeholders.{profile}: Absolute path of the profile.json /execution maintains (.execution/profile.json).
placeholders.{preview}: The local preview port the plan reserves for this project (unary resource port:{preview}).
placeholders.{workdir}: Absolute working directory of the task's lane (worktree or checkout), where fragment agents run their commands.
placeholders.{implementer_agent}: Agent type of /execution's implementers (execution-implementer); empty for the default workflow subagent.
placeholders.{build_prefix}: existing stack only: the project's build command followed by ' && ', or empty when the UI needs no build.
placeholders.{serve_target}: existing stack only: --serve "<built folder>", or --start "<command>" --url http://127.0.0.1:{preview}.

symbolic_depends.decision:project-name: The decision task in which the owner confirms the project name; dropped when profile.project.name_owner_confirmed is true. The logo spells the name, so FE-05 waits for it.
symbolic_depends.manual:harden-review: /execution's manual task in which the owner reviews and merges the /harden branch. FE-21 (H3) comes after it and before any recording task.

references.source: the plan: on unless the brief names no customer with a site or the UI budget cannot afford captures
references.description: on: FE-01 and FE-02 are instantiated and FE-03 depends on FE-02. off: both are dropped and FE-03 depends on FE-00; the directions then anchor in the protocol's domain, a utilitarian register and the customers' category as named in the brief.

mode.description: small (1-2 h of UI budget): estimate.small, one or two directions, a wordmark, one page built by a single FE-1x task after FE-09, at most one critique round.

vite-react.note: Default: Vite + React static build in {ui_root}/dist; frontend-check serves it on an ephemeral port. Every UI proof rebuilds {ui_root}/dist, so in /execution's single-tree workspace mode two UI tasks must not run their proofs at the same moment; worktrees and the verifier's clean checkouts are isolated.

next.note: Next 16, chosen only when the spec needs a server; frontend-check starts it on the preview port, waits for the URL, runs, then kills the process tree, so UI proofs take turns on that port.

static-html.note: Plain HTML and CSS (small mode, Origins): nothing to build, the folder is served as is.

existing.note: An app that already exists (BNB Holdover renders template strings from its own server): the planner reads its build and serve commands from the repository.

templates.title: Frontend brief
templates.description: Run brief.mjs to discover every input by glob from the workspace (the two sentences, the gap and who loses, sponsors and customers, the use case, the feature catalogue, the claims ledger, the never-show list, the judge's path) and write brief.json and brief.md in {state}, every field with the path (and line) it came from. A missing input goes under missing with action manual-task; a field is never guessed. Before T0 it runs with --state <workspace.private_dir>/frontend and makes no visual.

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min scaled by about 0.6: brief.mjs does the discovery and the agent checks sources. verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min (the proof reads files only).

proof.negative_control: Empty hero.source in {state}/brief.json while hero.h1 stays non-empty: brief.complete must fail.

templates.title: Confirm the reference sites (owner)
templates.description: The owner keeps, replaces or drops each reference URL the brief proposes from the sponsor's customers, so captures touch only confirmed official pages. The orchestrator records the answer in the profile's frontend.references (owner_confirmed), the list capture.mjs reads.

estimate.basis: Owner minutes once the push is read; no agent reference class applies, and the wait for the owner is scheduled by /execution from the latest start.

proof.expect: At least two entries with owner_confirmed true, each with an http(s) url and a non-empty source (in mode B the bare block's #/references).
proof.negative_control: A references list whose entries all have owner_confirmed false: the proof must fail and FE-02 stay blocked.

small_mode.note: Kept when references is on; two sites are enough in small mode.

steps: Open the customers section of {state}/brief.md: one proposed URL per customer, with where it came from.
For each customer, keep the URL if it is the customer's official site and its page closest to what we build; otherwise reply with the right page, or drop the customer.
If fewer than two unrelated references remain in the category, add sites you know: bot walls stop some captures, so 6-8 candidates per category is safer than 2 (FD19).
Name any site you know refuses robots or needs a login: it is captured from your own screenshots or notes, never by changing how the capture identifies itself.
manual.bring_back: One line per customer: keep <url> | replace <old url> -> <new url> | drop <customer>, plus any added site with its category. The orchestrator sets owner_confirmed in profile.frontend.references and records the reply.

templates.title: Reference captures and pattern ledger
templates.description: Capture one page of each confirmed reference site (2-4 sites) through capture-gate.mjs at the profile's viewports: viewport slices, a computed-style tally, the fonts that actually rendered, a reveal probe; robots.txt honoured, a stop on 401, 403, 407 or 429, no user-agent swap, stealth, proxy or retry after a block. Captures stay in {private_dir}/frontend/captures, outside any git work tree, with a SHA-256 manifest. extract.mjs writes the pattern ledger (conventions, relationships, domain conventions, facts, each from at least two unrelated references, nothing of a site's expression), then the captures are purged with a deletion receipt. A bot-walled site falls back to the owner's own notes, never to a workaround.

estimate.basis: /execution research class 13.0/24.9/40.6 min scaled by about 1.2 for three or four sites at three viewports; small mode captures two sites. verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min (the proof reads files only).

proof.negative_control: Delete one capture receipt listed in {state}/refs-index.json: refs.receipts must fail.

small_mode.note: Two sites instead of three or four.

templates.title: Directions: named token plans with hero comps
templates.description: The feDirections wave fragment draws 2-3 genuinely different named directions (1-2 in small mode) under {state}/directions/<A|B|C>/, each anchored in a different source (customer A, customer B, the protocol's domain, a utilitarian register), each a token plan (4-6 named colours with roles, type roles, radius and spacing, a motion budget, one signature element) plus one hero comp with the brief's real copy at 1440x900 and 390x844. Each direction is screened by the checker, by the similar-prompt test against a plan a fresh agent draws from a generic brief (written to {state}/similar-prompt/, outside directions/), and against the ledger of past directions; one that fails is redrawn once with the findings. board.mjs writes the board the orchestrator publishes for H1. No visual before T0 when the event forbids designs.

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min for directions drawn in parallel, plus a render and a screen per direction and one possible redraw; small mode draws one or two. verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min (the proof reads files only).

templates.title: Pick a direction (H1, owner)
templates.description: The owner picks one of the directions on the board. The frontend lane waits; every other lane keeps running.

covers.description: Owner checkpoint H1; covers no requirement.

estimate.basis: Owner minutes on the phone once the board is published; judges are near chance on close options, so the owner decides (FD17-F06, F16).

proof.expect: pick names a direction folder that exists under {state}/directions/ (A, B or C; a "none" answer, recorded with its reason, keeps the proof failing until a new round is picked), answered_at is UTC and channel is notion, remote-control, ask-user-question or terminal.
proof.negative_control: A choices.json without H1, or with a pick that has no folder under {state}/directions/: the proof must fail.

small_mode.note: Same checkpoint, one or two options.

steps: The orchestrator publishes the board from {state}/directions/ to the profile's review surface (references/03-directions.md, 'Publishing the board (orchestrator only)') and pushes the link.
Look at each direction's hero at desktop and phone size, its token plan, what it is anchored in and its trade-off.
Pick one direction by its letter. You may add one change in one sentence; anything larger is a new FE-03 run, not a change.
Answer through the Notion decision field or a Remote Control reply; comments on a Claude Design canvas are not answers.
manual.bring_back: The letter of the chosen direction (A, B or C) and at most one sentence of change. The orchestrator writes it to {state}/choices.json as H1 with the UTC time and the channel.

templates.title: Logo candidates, wordmark first
templates.description: brand.mjs draws 3-5 candidates (2-3 in small mode, wordmark only): the project name in an open-licensed face of the chosen direction (OFL.txt checked for a Reserved Font Name before any subset) with exactly one intervention, and a favicon mark derived from it on a 32-unit grid; a separate symbol only for a written reason. Each candidate is rendered at 16, 32, 180 and 512 px and as one-colour silhouettes on light and dark, and passes the mark lint (no gradient, no hexagon or cube, no <text>, strokes not thinner than viewBox/16, no struck-through initial). A model reviews defects only, at most 2-3 rounds, and never ranks; name and lookalike checks report only, never 'clear'.

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min: a scripted pipeline plus at most 2-3 defect-review rounds; small mode draws three wordmarks. verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min (the proof reads files only).

proof.negative_control: Delete the 16 px render of one candidate under {state}/brand/candidates/: brand.candidates must fail.

small_mode.note: Wordmark only, three candidates and one round (BR-09).

templates.title: Pick the logo (H2, owner)
templates.description: The owner picks one logo candidate; a model score never decides it (FD12-F09).

covers.description: Owner checkpoint H2; covers no requirement.

estimate.basis: Owner minutes on the phone once the logo board is published.

proof.expect: pick names a candidate folder that exists under {state}/brand/candidates/, answered_at is UTC and channel is notion, remote-control, ask-user-question or terminal.
proof.negative_control: A choices.json without H2, or with a pick that has no folder under {state}/brand/candidates/: the proof must fail.

steps: The orchestrator publishes the logo board from {state}/brand/candidates/ to the profile's review surface and pushes the link.
Judge each candidate first at 16 px and in one colour on light and dark, then at 180 and 512 px.
Pick one candidate by its number. You may add one change in one sentence.
Answer through the Notion decision field or a Remote Control reply; comments on a Claude Design canvas are not answers.
manual.bring_back: The number of the chosen candidate and at most one sentence of change. The orchestrator writes it to {state}/choices.json as H2 with the UTC time and the channel.

templates.title: Tokens and their generated views
templates.description: tokens.mjs builds {design}/tokens.json from the direction picked at H1 and the mark picked at H2: colour from the brand hue in OKLCH (Leonardo, contrast targets 3, 4.5 and 7) with a token-pair contrast table; at most two families plus a monospace with a role, self-hosted under {design}/fonts with their licence files and provenance entries, tabular figures checked for any face that shows numbers; spacing, radius, shadow and motion tokens (ease-out; press 100-160 ms, tooltip 125-200, dropdown 150-250, modal 200-300). It generates the CSS custom properties under {ui_root}/src/styles, the Tailwind @theme mirror after namespace resets when Tailwind is used, and DESIGN.md; none of these views is edited by hand.

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min scaled by about 0.75: tokens.mjs generates the views; the agent sets roles and usages. verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min (the proof reads files only).

proof.negative_control: Give one colour token in {design}/tokens.json an empty usage: tokens.valid must fail.

small_mode.note: Same tokens file, fewer type styles.

templates.title: App shell and first screen
templates.description: Scaffold the UI package at {ui_root} on the profile's stack (no starter-template leftovers, no prebuilt wallet-connect UI), import the generated token CSS, carry the mark picked at H2 in the header, and build the first-screen contract: an H1 of about 2-6 words and the sentence from brief.hero marked data-hero, one sourced live figure (data-metric with data-ledger or data-source and data-as-of), the sponsor named in text, and the product itself visible (data-surface="product"), with nothing important behind hover. Write {design}/routes.json mapping every catalogue feature id to a route, and create one empty mount point per feature group under {ui_root}/src/sections/<group>/ so FE-1x tasks write only inside their own folder. Support record mode (?record=1) and, when the profile sets ready_flag, window.__FRONTEND_READY__.

covers.description: Shell and first screen; feature surfaces are covered by FE-1x.

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min plus the scaffold and one install (manifest resource). verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min plus a build and a browser run.

proof.negative_control: Change the text of the element marked data-hero="h1" so it no longer equals brief.hero.h1: coverage.hero must fail.

small_mode.note: One static page; its sections are built by the single FE-1x task.

templates.title: Brand files, favicon set and OG image
templates.description: From the mark picked at H2, brand.mjs writes brand/ (mark.svg in currentColor, mono, lockup, a README with the meaning, the font licence and the provenance), favicon.ico with one 32 px entry, icon.svg with a prefers-color-scheme rule that survives SVGO (inlineStyles false), apple-touch-icon 180, manifest icons 192 and 512 and a maskable 512 with a computed safe radius, og.png 1200x630, the head links (index.html for Vite or a static page; the app folder's file conventions for Next), the deletion of any template favicon, the provenance entries and the drift test (references/04-brand.md, steps 9 to 11). It touches no section. This template fills the gap between H2 and the build: ARCHITECTURE.md 12.1 names no task for the brand deliverables, yet --phase build gates them.

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min scaled by about 0.45: the pipeline is scripted (FD12 measured 6.2 s for the whole Node pipeline). verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min plus a build and a browser run.

proof.negative_control: Replace {ui_root}/public/icon.svg with a copy that has no prefers-color-scheme rule: brand.icon-dark must fail.

small_mode.note: Kept in small mode: the wordmark still gets its favicon set and OG card, gated by this task's own proof; --phase small (FE-20) does not gate brand files.

templates.title: Section for feature group {group}
templates.description: Build the surface of every feature of {group} ({features}) inside {ui_root}/src/sections/{group}/: for each feature id a heading in the user's words, a visible surface marked data-feature, its status label (data-status live, testnet, simulated or planned) and its proof (a claims-ledger id, a middle-truncated transaction link checked by rendering, or a live value with its as-of time); transaction lifecycle, loading, empty and error states that say what to do; copy from the brief with verbs that say what happens; motion only for real state changes. Every rendered number carries data-ledger or data-source. No new dependency and no new asset file: provenance.json belongs to FE-07 and FE-09.

covers.description: Covers the FR ids of {group}, and depends on every non-frontend task whose covers intersect them (the feature's own build task).

estimate.basis: /execution build class 6.2/26.7/46.0 min per feature group; small mode builds every feature on one page in one task. verify: /execution verify class 1.6/6.7/31.1 min plus a build and a browser run.

proof.negative_control: Delete the data-feature root of one id of {group}: coverage.features must fail.

small_mode.note: One task for every group ({group} = all, {features} = every catalogue id), after FE-09, because one static page is one file.

templates.title: Critique rounds and final gates
templates.description: The feCritique wave fragment measures the built UI (the gates of its proof phase, --phase build in full mode and --phase small in small mode, deterministic sub-scores, DOM-marked tiles at 1440x900 and 390x844), then runs at most rounds_max rounds (1 in small mode) of three fresh frontend-critic passes. An issue is kept only if two critics raise it or a deterministic check confirms it, at most five per round, each with a mark id, the measured problem and a concrete fix. A candidate replaces the best-so-far only when every gate still passes, no deterministic sub-score drops and it wins the pairwise comparison in both orders; otherwise the tree goes back to the best-so-far. It stops after two rejected candidates, or when no issue is kept (CR-11). Five blind frontend-probe readers per viewport must restate the brief's proposition (at least 4 of 5). The receipt is written to {state}/critique/receipt.json and the rendered UI copy to {state}/ui-copy.md for /prose.

covers.description: Quality gate over every surface; covers no requirement itself.

estimate.basis: Multi-agent: per round about 25-40 min (measure, three critics in parallel, one fix, measure, two pairwise judges, probes after an accept), up to rounds_max rounds, stopping early when no issue is kept. Each agent stays under about 20 min, so /execution's 60 min single-agent sizing rule does not apply to the total; small mode runs one round. verify: /execution verify class plus the receipt check and the full --phase build run.

proof.negative_control: Set ok to false in {state}/critique/receipt.json, or delete the file: the receipt check must exit 1.

small_mode.note: At most one round; the proof runs --phase small (render, a11y, coverage, firstview, tells, ip), through --phase {mode}.

templates.title: Sign off the deployed preview at recording size (H3, owner)
templates.description: After /harden's review, the owner signs off the deployed preview at the size it will be recorded, before any recording task. A no reopens work as fix tasks; it is never recorded as a sign-off.

covers.description: Owner checkpoint H3; covers no requirement.

estimate.basis: Owner minutes at the laptop: one walk through the judge's path at recording size; the best measured judges still trail humans by about 14 points (FD17-F07).

proof.expect: signed_off is true with an empty changes list, answered_at is UTC and channel is notion, remote-control, ask-user-question or terminal.
proof.negative_control: An H3 with signed_off false and a numbered list of changes: the proof must fail and every recording task stay blocked.

steps: On the laptop, open the deployed preview with ?record=1 in a browser window of 1536x864 CSS px at 125% zoom, the recording setup (FD20).
Walk the judge's path from the brief: the first screen, then every feature section; each shows its status label (live, testnet, simulated or planned) and its proof.
Read the latest gate report under {state}/gates/ and the critique receipt {state}/critique/receipt.json: every gate ok, none skipped, probes passed.
Check that nothing on the never-show list appears in images or frames (the gates checked the rendered text).
Sign off, or list what must change before anything is recorded.
manual.bring_back: signed off: yes, or no with a numbered list of changes, each naming the screen and what is wrong. The orchestrator writes it to {state}/choices.json as H3 with the preview URL, the UTC time and the channel.
